candidates.name: Minervini Trend Template + breakout
candidates.source: Minervini, Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard (McGraw-Hill, 2013), Trend Template (8 criteria)
candidates.notes: Full 8-criterion template. Criterion 8 uses derived_rs_rank (in-universe), NOT IBD's rating: percentile (0-100) of the 252-session return within the eligible universe on the same bar; missing history -> criterion 8 not_evaluable (rs_rank_unavailable) for that stock only.

candidates.name: Connors RSI(2) in uptrend
candidates.source: Connors & Alvarez, Short Term Trading Strategies That Work (2008), 2-period RSI
candidates.notes: No stop in the published rule; risk is carried by position size and the fast SMA5 exit.

candidates.name: Bollinger squeeze breakout (Method I)
candidates.source: Bollinger, Bollinger on Bollinger Bands (McGraw-Hill, 2001), %b / BandWidth / Squeeze
candidates.notes: Squeeze = BandWidth lowest in 126 sessions within the last 5 sessions; breakout gives direction.

candidates.name: Wilder ADX/DMI trend
candidates.source: Wilder, New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems (1978), Directional Movement System
candidates.notes: Entry is +DI crossing above -DI with ADX(14) > 25 (plan text). Wilder's extreme-point rule is NOT applied (daily-close harness).

candidates.name: 12-1 cross-sectional momentum (adapted)
candidates.source: Jegadeesh & Titman, "Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers", Journal of Finance 48(1), 65-91 (1993)
candidates.notes: ADAPTED, not the paper's exact rule: the paper is cross-sectional (rank all stocks, buy the top decile); this single-name version ranks the Track A universe by 12-1 return. Rank is evaluated at monthly rebalances (first session of each month) in a state-aware walk; the 63-session hold expiry comes from the actual entry only. Needs the full universe panel.

candidates.name: Sector-adjusted 12-1 momentum (top 30)
candidates.source: Ceta Research, "Sector-adjusted momentum, India (BSE/NSE, 2000-2025)"; Jegadeesh & Titman, "Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers", Journal of Finance 48(1), 65-91 (1993)
candidates.notes: Sector-adjusted variant of 12-1 momentum: rank by the 12-1 return MINUS the stock's sector average 12-1 return; buy the top 30 at each monthly rebalance, exit at the next rebalance when the stock drops out of the top 30. No 63-session expiry (the published sector-adjusted rule has none). Different ranking from C105 (whole-market rank), so not a duplicate of C105. Needs the full universe panel AND a symbol->sector map (explicit sector_map, or a sector/industry column on the universe frame); with no usable map it enters nothing.

candidates.name: Dual MA crossover (S4) + ATR-based position sizing
candidates.source: MUSE-PLAN-adaptive-risk-fixes.md §3 (risk plan, 2026-11-22); S4 = frozen strategy_4 (EMA20/50 cross with SMA200)

initial_stop.definition: No fixed stop; exits are indicator-based (see exits). Reporting R uses the 2x ATR(14)-based 1R convention (plan §4.4, Grok Q3).

candidates.notes: Mirrors S4 exactly (EMA20/50 cross-up above SMA200 for entry, cross-down for exit) plus ATR-based sizing: qty = risk budget / (2 x ATR(14) at entry), capped so qty x entry price never exceeds Rs 50,000 per trade. Risk budget Rs 5,000 = 1% of the Rs 5,00,000 sleeve capital — a CHOICE, not a policy value, flagged for Senior/Grok to confirm. The Rs 50,000 per-trade maximum and the Rs 5 lakh per-strategy cap do not change. Risk per trade is the budget when the ATR formula binds, less when the value cap binds (very stable stocks). First candidate with ATR-based sizing; the other candidates use the frozen Rs 50,000 fixed sizing.
